newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says 49 killed in Kurdish rebel conflict.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says 49 killed in Kurdish rebel conflict.

text.p: Forty-nine combatants in Turkey's Kurdish rebel conflict have been killed in separate clashes in recent days, security officials said on Saturday.

The regional governor's office in the city of Diyarbakir said in a statement that 42 Kurdistan Workers Party guerrillas had died in the last three days in clashes in the provinces of Sirnak, Siirt, Batman, Hakkari and Diyarbakir.
It said three village guards had died in the fighting and that four members of the security forces had been killed when a rebel mine exploded near the Iraqi border.
Witnesses have reported a build up of troops near the mountainous border with Iraq in the past few weeks in a sign of a possible cross-border drive against rebel camps there.
Defence Minister Turhan Tayan said on Saturday that Turkey would not tolerate the rebels' presence in north Iraq.
"Nobody should expect us to be a spectator to the terrorist threat that has come about because of the power vacuum in northern Iraq," Anatolian news agency quoted him as saying.
Northern Iraq is controlled by Iraqi Kurdish groups that took over the area after Baghdad's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War.
But Tayan said Turkey would not go into Iraq without good reason. "We will not cross the border unless we have to, unless there is a need to pusruse (rebels)," he said.

More than 22,000 people have been killed in 12 years of fighting between Turkish security forces and the guerrillas, Turkey was criticised by some of its Western allies for a six-week drive into northern Iraq involving 35,000 men in 1995.
